coverage.remaining: Nothing of the lists in curiv_elderwood_ver02 is known to remain unread: every issue of 16 December 1912 - 15 July 1913 it holds (196 issues, 5,877 pages) was scanned, 480 page-blocks on 168 days located and read whole. 1-15 February 1913 is in curiv_dardanelle_ver01 and was read in the September 2026 pass; 16 July - 8 December 1913 is in curiv_grimes_ver01, also read; 9-31 December 1913 is in no batch. Of the 611 unresolved, 306 not measurable, 155 no parcel with a roll year that fits, 104 single candidates refused, 23 on a street EAS does not join, 15 other, 5 several parcels match, 2 prints a number whose building is gone, 1 a condominium parcel.
coverage.note: 5,877 OCR pages scanned (every page of 16 December 1912 - 15 July 1913 in curiv_elderwood_ver02, a batch the dossier's table had filed under 1900-1905 unmapped). 480 page-blocks kept - 310 located by heading, entry shape and a storey count near a location word, 170 more by a sweep of the real-estate pages' untrimmed spans, which the located pass missed where mid-1913's OCR loses the heading and the dollar signs. 754 contract entries read by ten readers from one spec, 1,017 candidate paragraphs read and rejected as deeds, advertisements, loan and market news or fragments with no location; 23 reprints folded into the entry they repeat - 731 findings (668 building contracts, 63 alterations). 120 resolved by hand on 93 parcels: 116 by lot, offset and corner with corner.py --batch --json and its centreline test, 4 on a printed number checked against the roll's year. 611 unresolved, each with its reason. 91 published on 91 pages; 29 declined: 27 further contracts for a building whose entry already carries one, 2 contradicting what the page already records.

notes: The San Francisco Call's daily Building Contracts list for 16 December 1912 to 15 July 1913, from curiv_elderwood_ver02. Located on the 1906-1912 shapes - the heading however the OCR mangles it, the entry's own 'with CONTRACTOR - WORK ... line/corner of ...; $AMOUNT', and a storey count within 200 characters of 'line of'/'corner of' - plus a third shape this year needed: an amount over $100 with a location and a building word in the 450 characters before it, kept only where three such amounts cluster. Mid-1913's OCR interleaves the column with timetables and loses both the heading and the dollar signs, so the located pass alone missed whole lists (24 December 1912, 29 May, 13 June 1913): every real-estate page (10 or more 'lot in' phrases, or two work-and-storey phrases) was swept for contract paragraphs outside the located blocks, and the sweep found 170 more blocks. The list prints the owner before 'with', so each quote starts at 'with' and ends at the entry's own amount; private owners, estates and trustees appear nowhere in the file, institutional and company owners in extra.owner_firm and a named building in extra.building_name. Every quote was re-anchored on the block's own text after reading, so raw is verbatim OCR; 25 quotes the anchor could not confirm were left as the reader wrote them, and every quote's head and tail was scanned for a name. Streets mapped onto EAS's own spellings (First avenue is Arguello, Thirteenth avenue Funston, Point Lobos Geary, Dupont Grant, Montgomery avenue Columbus, Army Cesar Chavez, the lettered Sunset and Richmond streets by the 1909 key); a numbered street carries the type the record prints, and one printed with no type was tried both ways and kept only where exactly one meets the main street. Placed with corner.py --batch --json: a lot pass, an offset pass and a corner pass, on 1913 for new work and built_by for an alteration, with the centreline test this run moved out of the 1906 session script and into the tool. A candidate needed its roll year, the side or quadrant the record names by both tests, its offset within 4 ft where the record gives one, and storeys within one and a half; a corner record whose printed lot could not be measured needed its storeys to agree exactly. One parcel is one page, and one entry per building: the general contract, else the earliest, carries the page's entry and the rest are declined. Of the 21 entries that print a street number, 4 resolved against the roll's year and 2 were refused because the roll dates the building there later than the alteration.
